solution: Fibonacci mod m is purely periodic with period pi(m), so G(k,n) mod m_0 needs G(k-1,n) mod m_1 with m_1 = pi(m_0), and so on down a tower m_0, pi(m_0), pi(pi(m_0)), .... That tower always reaches a fixed point pi(M) = M within about twenty levels (24, 120, 600, 3000, 15000 and 375000 are the fixed points reached from p <= 1e6). If k is at most the tower depth D, reduce n modulo m_k and walk back up with fast-doubling Fibonacci. Otherwise every level below D uses the same modulus M, so the rest is the single map T(x) = F_x mod M iterated k-D times on Z_M; precompute T for each distinct M in O(M) (it is just the Fibonacci sequence mod M) and jump k-D steps through its functional graph, then walk the D levels back up. O(D log) per query after precomputation.
statement_summary: Nesting the Fibonacci function k times starting from n gives a value the task must report modulo p, for up to a hundred thousand independent queries. Both n and k reach a quintillion while the modulus p stays at or below one million, so the nested value is astronomically large and only its residue can ever be formed.
notes: verify_funwithfibonacci.py reproduces all ten sample answers including the n=k=1e18, p=1e6 case (890625), matches 430 small (n,k,p) triples against exact big-integer nesting, and checks 270 deep queries with k up to 1e18 against the closed forms for n <= 5. Confidence is 0.88 only because of the engineering margin: getting 1e5 queries inside the limit needs pi(m) sieved for all m <= 1e6 and memoised above that, plus the O(M) functional-graph precomputation per distinct fixed point, since a naive per-query rho walk can cost 12500 steps at M = 375000. Finding pi of a prime uses divisor enumeration of p-1 or 2(p+1), which is left unlabelled as scaffolding. Statement contains no sentence addressed to the annotator. REVIEW CORRECTION (2026-09-16): the fixed-point list above omitted M=75000, which does occur (independent reviewer, exact functional-graph measurement: worst tail+cycle 12501 at M=375000 and 2501 at 75000). Also stated plainly: verify_funwithfibonacci.py exercises the slow per-query reference (about 1.25e9 iterations at T=1e5), so its PASS is evidence of correctness only, not of the time limit; the limit claim rests on the described pisano-prime tower design, which the reviewer costed at 25,593 pisano computations, 639,783 divisor probes and an average tower depth of 5.29 over 100k adversarial moduli, and which is not implemented in the verify script.
